english: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=[x]\,\{x\}$, where $[t]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$ and $\{t\}=t-[t]$. For a real number $k<0$, the area of the region bounded by the curve $y=f(x)$, the $x$-axis and the lines $x=k$ and $x=4$ is $\dfrac{21}{2}$. Then the value of $k$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=[x]\,\{x\}$ द्वारा परिभाषित है, जहाँ $[t]$, $t$ से छोटा या उसके बराबर महत्तम पूर्णांक है तथा $\{t\}=t-[t]$ है। किसी वास्तविक संख्या $k<0$ के लिए, वक्र $y=f(x)$, $x$-अक्ष तथा रेखाओं $x=k$ एवं $x=4$ द्वारा परिबद्ध क्षेत्र का क्षेत्रफल $\dfrac{21}{2}$ है। तब $k$ का मान ______ है।
solution: On $[n,n+1)$: $f(x)=n(x-n)$, a segment from $0$ to $n$; it is below the axis for $n<0$, so each unit piece contributes $\left|\displaystyle\int_{n}^{n+1}n(x-n)dx\right|=\dfrac{|n|}{2}$.
Area over $[-m,0]$ ($m$ a positive integer) $=\dfrac{1+2+\dots+m}{2}=\dfrac{m(m+1)}{4}$; $m=5$ gives $\dfrac{15}{2}$. The area increases strictly as $k$ decreases, so $k=-5$ is the only value.
solution_full: For $n\le x<n+1$ ($n$ an integer): $[x]=n$, $\{x\}=x-n$, so $f(x)=n(x-n)$, a straight segment rising (or falling) from $0$ at $x=n$ towards $n$ at $x=n+1$.

For $n>0$ the piece is above the $x$-axis, for $n<0$ below it, and for $n=0$ it is on the axis. The area of each piece is therefore $\left|\displaystyle\int_{n}^{n+1}n(x-n)dx\right|=\dfrac{|n|}{2}$ (a triangle of base 1 and height $|n|$).
Over $[k,0]$ with $k<0$: each full piece $n=-1,-2,\ldots$ adds $\dfrac{|n|}{2}$; the area is a continuous, strictly increasing function of $|k|$ (every piece with $n\le -1$ has positive area).
For $k=-m$ ($m$ a positive integer) the area over $[k,0]$ is $\dfrac{1+2+\cdots+m}{2}=\dfrac{m(m+1)}{4}$. We need $\dfrac{21}{2}-3=\dfrac{15}{2}$, i.e. $m(m+1)=30$, $m=5$.
By strict monotonicity no other $k$ works, so $k=-5$.
originality_note: New: the sawtooth with growing amplitude f(x) = [x]{x}, whose pieces flip below the axis for negative x, with the lower limit recovered from a total area (way 5). Closest known: integral of [x] or {x} over an interval. Different because: the product makes each piece a triangle of height |n| and the sign change for n < 0 must be handled as area, not as a signed integral.

concept_use.Areas involving GIF, fractional part or: On [n, n+1), f = n(x - n) is a segment; each piece is a triangle of area |n|/2.
concept_use.Area bounded by a curve and the x-axis;: Pieces with n < 0 lie below the axis, so their areas are |n|/2, not n/2; the signed integral would give a different k.
